title: Grade 11 Physics — Applications of Newton's Laws & Friction
description: Connected bodies, inclined planes, friction types, and circular motion forces
subject: physics

questions.question: Two masses m₁ = 5 kg and m₂ = 3 kg are connected by a string over a frictionless pulley (Atwood machine). The acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Atwood machine: a = (m₁−m₂)g/(m₁+m₂) = (5−3)×10/(5+3) = 20/8 = 2.5 m/s². In terms of g: a = 2g/8 = g/4.

questions.question: A block of mass 5 kg on a frictionless inclined plane (angle 30°) accelerates down. The acceleration is: (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: On a frictionless incline: a = g sinθ = 10 × sin30° = 10 × 0.5 = 5 m/s². The normal force = mg cosθ (perpendicular to slope).

questions.question: Static friction is the friction that:
options: Acts when the object is in motion
Acts on a stationary object about to move, opposing the applied force (up to maximum value μₛN)
Is always less than kinetic friction
Acts only on rough surfaces in motion
questions.explanation: Static friction prevents relative motion between surfaces at rest. It increases with applied force up to a maximum f_s = μₛN (μₛ = coefficient of static friction). Beyond this, kinetic friction takes over.

questions.question: Kinetic friction is typically _____ static friction for the same surfaces.
questions.explanation: μₖ (kinetic) < μₛ (static) for the same pair of surfaces. This is why it is harder to START sliding an object than to KEEP it sliding once moving.

questions.question: A 10 kg block on a rough surface (μₖ = 0.3) is pushed with 50 N. Kinetic friction force is: (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Normal force N = mg = 10 × 10 = 100 N. Kinetic friction fₖ = μₖ × N = 0.3 × 100 = 30 N.

questions.question: A block on an incline of angle θ is on the verge of sliding. The coefficient of static friction is:
options: sin θ / cos θ = tan θ
questions.explanation: At the verge of sliding on incline: f_s = mg sinθ and N = mg cosθ. μₛ = f_s/N = (mg sinθ)/(mg cosθ) = tan θ. This angle is called the 'angle of friction'.

questions.question: The centripetal force for a car going around a banked curve is provided by:
options: The horizontal component of the normal force (and friction for speeds away from optimal)
questions.explanation: On a banked curve: the normal force N acts perpendicular to the banked road. Its horizontal component N sinθ provides centripetal force. This allows cars to turn without friction at the optimal speed.

questions.question: Two blocks of mass 3 kg and 5 kg are in contact on a frictionless surface. A force of 16 N is applied on the 3 kg block. The contact force between the blocks is:
questions.explanation: System acceleration: a = 16/(3+5) = 2 m/s². Contact force on 5 kg block: F = ma = 5 × 2 = 10 N. (The contact force accelerates only the 5 kg block.)

questions.question: Pseudo force (fictitious force) arises in:
questions.explanation: In a non-inertial frame (accelerating reference frame), Newton's laws appear violated. To apply them, we add a pseudo force = −ma (opposite to the frame's acceleration). Examples: force felt in a braking car.

questions.question: The minimum speed at the top of a vertical circular loop for a body to maintain contact is: (radius R)
questions.explanation: At the top of the loop: minimum speed v_min = √(gR). At this speed, centripetal force = gravity (N = 0, just losing contact). Minimum speed at bottom of loop = √(5gR).

questions.question: Rolling friction is _____ sliding friction because:
options: Greater than; rolling deforms surfaces more
Less than; only small deformation occurs at the rolling contact point
Equal to; friction depends only on surface roughness
Unrelated to; they follow different laws
questions.explanation: Rolling friction << sliding friction. In rolling, only the contact point momentarily deforms — much less energy is lost. This is why wheels were invented: replacing sliding with rolling massively reduces friction.

questions.question: A block of mass 2 kg on a rough incline (30°, μₖ = 0.2) is sliding down. Net acceleration is: (g = 10 m/s²)
The angle of banking θ for a road curve of radius R at optimal speed v is:
questions.explanation: Optimal banking: tan θ = v²/Rg. At this speed, no friction is needed. Example: v = 20 m/s, R = 100 m, g = 10: tan θ = 400/1000 = 0.4 → θ ≈ 21.8°.

questions.question: If a person pushes a wall, the wall pushes back with equal and opposite force. This is Newton's:
questions.explanation: Newton's Third Law: for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. Action-reaction pairs act on DIFFERENT bodies — person pushes wall (action on wall), wall pushes person (reaction on person).

questions.question: A 1000 kg car rounds a flat circular track (radius 50 m) at 20 m/s. Centripetal force needed is:
questions.explanation: Centripetal force F = mv²/r = 1000 × (20)² / 50 = 1000 × 400/50 = 8000 N. This force must be provided by friction on a flat track.
